posts.excerpt: A practical framework for comparing residency options before you commit time, money, and paperwork.
posts.body:
International relocation decisions are easiest when you separate **strategy** from **paperwork**.

## Start with constraints
Before choosing a destination, map your real constraints:

- Budget ceiling for year one
- Family, school, or health priorities
- Work model (remote employee, freelancer, founder)
- Timeline and urgency

## Compare pathways objectively
Shortlist countries, then score each on:

1. Legal residency clarity
2. Tax exposure and reporting burden
3. Cost of compliance and setup
4. Stability and long-term flexibility

## Decide before filing
A strong strategy means fewer expensive surprises later. In most cases, better planning up front reduces legal and administrative rework after the move.
posts.title: How to Choose a Cross-Border Residency Strategy
